output.argument_summary: The admissible record does not support a controls-only theory of certification. It does support a narrower position: aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and the 3% rollout with rollback and monitoring provides operational containment, while the exposed health-plan benefits support weakness remains a material limitation that must be disclosed at launch under the stated policy. The correct interpretation is therefore not unconditional compliance, but caveated certification support conditioned on treating launch-time disclosure as part of the certification basis rather than claiming rollout controls cure the weakness.

output.claims_about_policy: The policy text cuts against the overbroad claim that small-percentage rollout, rollback, and monitoring eliminate disclosure duties. At the same time, the same policy does not foreclose certification if the material limitation is disclosed at launch; it forecloses certification without disclosure, exclusion of the affected use case, or approved risk acceptance. On the present admissible record, the supportable policy claim is that certification is only conditionally supportable and should be evaluated as caveated rather than as a flat policy violation cured by controls.
